questions.question: Why is using `push` with `shift` a poor choice for a large queue in JavaScript?
options: shift returns elements in LIFO order
shift generally moves every remaining element, so draining n items costs O(n²)
push is O(n) on large arrays
Arrays cannot hold more than 65,536 elements
questions.explanation: Removing the front element shifts the rest down. A head-index queue or a linked list avoids moving elements and keeps dequeue O(1).

questions.question: In the two-stack queue, when should elements be moved from the `in` stack to the `out` stack?
options: On every dequeue, regardless of the out stack
Only when the out stack is empty
Only when the in stack is full
questions.explanation: Refilling only when out is empty preserves FIFO order and ensures each element moves once, giving amortised O(1) dequeue.

questions.question: A bracket checker pushes opening brackets and pops on closing ones, but returns true as soon as the loop ends. Which input does it wrongly accept?
questions.explanation: "((" never triggers a mismatch, but two brackets remain open. The final `stack.length === 0` check is what rejects it.

questions.question: How does the MinStack return the minimum in O(1)?
options: It sorts the items on every push
It scans the items array from the top
It stores the minimum in a single variable updated on push
It keeps a parallel stack where each entry is the minimum of all items at or below that level
questions.explanation: A single variable cannot be restored after popping the minimum. The parallel stack remembers the minimum at every level, so pop restores it automatically.
